instruction: In the spreadsheet, use a formula in cell E2 to count how many numeric values are present in column A (from A2 to A20).

metadata.explanation: Task requires counting numeric values in column A (A2:A20) using a COUNT or COUNTA formula in cell E2. Verified with Python: column A contains 19 numeric values (rows 2-20). Evaluator reads both the formula and calculated value from cell E2 after saving. The getter extracts both formula text and calculated value. The metric verifies: (1) a formula exists in E2, (2) the formula contains COUNT/COUNTA, (3) the formula references range A2:A20, and (4) the calculated value equals 19. This ensures the agent uses a formula rather than hardcoding the value.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: formula existence, COUNT function usage, correct range A2:A20, and correct calculated value
Getter logic is correct: uses openpyxl with data_only=False to extract formula text, then data_only=True to get calculated value from cell E2
Metric logic is sound: checks (1) formula exists, (2) contains COUNT/COUNTA, (3) references A2:A20 range, (4) calculated value equals 19 with numeric tolerance
Complete instruction coverage: verifies both the process (formula usage) and the outcome (correct result)
Expected value 19 is verified correct per metadata explanation
Appropriate postconfig: saves file with Ctrl+S to persist formula and ensure it can be read
Edge cases handled: None values, type checking, numeric tolerance for float comparison
